# Realtime Location Tracker

> A high-performance, real-time geolocation tracking system built with Node.js, Express, Socket.IO, Leaflet.js, and WebRTC.

## Overview

The Realtime Location Tracker is a modular web application designed to capture real-time spatial updates via HTML5 Geolocation APIs and transmit coordinates and metadata securely using WebSockets (`Socket.IO`). Connected client locations are plotted dynamically on an interactive map rendered via `Leaflet.js` with support for multiple tile layers (OpenStreetMap, Satellite, Dark Mode, Topo, CyclOSM, etc.), room-scoped live chat, peer-to-peer WebRTC voice calling, battery monitoring, emergency SOS alerts, and progressive web application (PWA) offline capabilities.

## Key Features

- **Realtime Bidirectional Communication:** Low-latency WebSocket connections via Socket.IO with HMAC-signed session verification and per-event sliding window rate limiting.
- **Adaptive Geolocation Tracking:** Intelligent geolocation polling with accelerometer-driven motion detection (switches between active and idle modes to conserve battery).
- **Interactive Mapping:** Interactive map visualization powered by Leaflet.js with customized, accessible high-contrast device markers, accuracy estimates, and fit-bounds.
- **Room Scoping & Privacy:** Namespace-isolated rooms (default `public`), easy invite sharing via link, and instant location pause/resume controls.
- **Room-Scoped Chat:** Real-time text messaging with sender attribution and click-to-focus on the map.
- **P2P Voice Communication:** WebRTC mesh audio calling with microphone mute/unmute and room invite announcements.
- **Emergency SOS Relay:** Hold-to-trigger emergency alert relay with multiple location fallbacks, honest delivery indicators, and audio/visual alerts.
- **Fleet Battery Monitoring:** Real-time tracking of device battery levels and charging states with low/critical power alerts.
- **Progressive Web App (PWA):** Service worker precaching, offline fallback notice page, and installation support across desktop and mobile.

## Tech Stack

### Backend & Middleware
- **Runtime:** Node.js (v18+ recommended, v20/v22 LTS supported)
- **Framework:** Express.js (HTTP server hosting & static asset delivery with compression, helmet CSP, and rate limiting)
- **Realtime Layer:** Socket.IO v4 (WebSocket transport with CORS controls and HMAC-signed session authorization)
- **View Engine:** EJS (Embedded JavaScript)

### Frontend & Client Tools
- **Mapping Library:** Leaflet.js (Self-hosted assets)
- **Tiles Providers:** OpenStreetMap, Esri Satellite, CartoDB Dark/Light/Voyager, OpenTopoMap, CyclOSM
- **Realtime Client:** Socket.IO Client SDK v4
- **Audio / Signaling:** WebRTC (RTCPeerConnection + STUN servers)
- **Styling & Fonts:** Responsive CSS with Glassmorphism, CSS Custom Properties, and self-hosted Font Awesome 6
- **Storage:** LocalStorage for user preferences (theme, profile, paused sharing state, SOS local history)

## Architecture & Data Flow

1. **Connection Initialization:**
   - Client requests `/` via HTTP; Express validates or signs an anonymous session cookie (`sid`) using HMAC-SHA256.
   - Server renders the EJS template containing the map canvas, UI controls, and client modules.
   - Client opens an authenticated WebSocket upgrade using the signed session cookie.
   - Client emits `join-room` with room name and nickname.

2. **Position Tracking & Emission:**
   - Geolocation coordinates are captured using `navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition`.
   - Motion detection adjusts polling between active (`LOCATION_SEND_INTERVAL` = 2s) and stationary (`LOCATION_IDLE_INTERVAL` = 30s).
   - Minimal movement threshold (8m) avoids redundant updates.
   - Client emits `send-location` with latitude, longitude, estimated accuracy, and sanitized device info.

3. **Broadcasting & Rendering:**
   - Server verifies coordinates, rate limits, and broadcasts to room members via `receive-location`.
   - Connected clients update their local `markers` map dictionary and room device lists.

4. **Emergency SOS & Audio Signaling:**
   - SOS alerts are relayed to connected room members with server-verified timestamps, IP info, and delivery acknowledgements.
   - WebRTC SDP offers/answers and ICE candidates are validated and forwarded between audio participants in the room.

5. **Disconnection Lifecycle:**
   - On disconnect or room leave, server emits `user-disconnect` and `user-disconnected`.
   - Client cleans up map marker pins and closes peer audio connections.

## File Structure

```text
Realtime-Location-Tracker/
├── public/
│   ├── assets/            # Device icons, favicons, audio icons, and graphics
│   ├── css/               # Modular CSS (workspace, panel, device, chat, audio, sos, etc.)
│   ├── js/                # ES modules (main, map, socket, controls, audio, chat, sos, etc.)
│   ├── vendor/            # Self-hosted Leaflet and Font Awesome
│   ├── manifest.json      # PWA manifest
│   ├── offline.html       # Offline fallback page
│   └── sw.js              # Service Worker implementation
├── src/
│   ├── middleware/        # Express middleware (Helmet, CSP, Compression, Rate Limit)
│   ├── routes/            # HTTP routes (/health, /, /developer, session verification)
│   ├── sockets/           # Socket.IO handlers, validation, rate limiting, and room logic
│   ├── views/             # EJS templates (index.ejs, 404.ejs, error.ejs)
│   └── app.js             # Express app & HTTP/Socket.IO server bootstrap
├── tests/
│   ├── routes.test.js     # HTTP routes and session signing tests
│   ├── sockets.test.js    # Socket.IO event handler and security tests
│   └── browser/           # Playwright responsive workspace interaction tests
├── scripts/
│   ├── check-syntax.js    # Cross-platform JavaScript syntax validator
│   └── check-syntax.sh    # Shell wrapper for CI
├── Dockerfile             # Production container definition
├── docker-compose.yml     # Container orchestration
├── package.json           # Project manifest and scripts
├── AUDIT.md               # Security audit and engineering notes
└── README.md              # Documentation
```

## Setup & Running Instructions

### Prerequisites
- Node.js (v18.x, v20.x, or v22.x)
- npm (v9+)

### Installation & Test
```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/mahmud-r-farhan/Realtime-Location-Tracker.git
cd Realtime-Location-Tracker

# Install dependencies cleanly
npm ci

# Run syntax check across all JavaScript files
npm run check

# Run unit and integration tests
npm test

# Run browser interaction tests
npm run test:browser
```

### Execution
```bash
# Start in production mode
npm start

# Or development mode with auto-reload
npm run dev
```

Default server port: `http://localhost:3007` (configurable via `PORT` environment variable).
